fields.acceptance: Testscripts run rhiza check with no check.json, with check.json lacking unclaimed_since, and with an unresolvable hash: the first two report no unclaimed finding and exit 0 on an otherwise clean repo with untrailered commits, the third fails with a message naming .rhiza/check.json
fields.statement: rhiza check reads the unclaimed-changes cutoff from an optional committed .rhiza/check.json, {"unclaimed_since": "<full commit hash>"}: no file or no key turns the rule off, and a hash that does not resolve to a commit is a check error naming the file; repo.json is untouched

fields.acceptance: A testscript with a cutoff commits: one code commit with no trailer, one whose Change: names an unknown ID, one with a known Change: in a paragraph before Co-Authored-By, one touching only .rhiza/, one with only Actor:/Leaf: trailers, a merge commit, and one untrailered commit before the cutoff; check --json lists exactly one warn finding of the unclaimed rule for the first, second and fifth, each naming its commit and saying missing or unknown, and exits 0
fields.statement: With a cutoff set, rhiza check warns once on each non-merge commit in <cutoff>..HEAD that changes a file outside .rhiza/ and has no Change: trailer (read by parseTrailerLog) naming a change set in the log, saying whether the trailer is missing or names an unknown change set; Actor:, Leaf: and Review: trailers alone do not claim a commit

fields.acceptance: .rhiza/check.json in the change set's commit holds the full hash of a commit on origin/main that is an ancestor of the branch, and make self-check runs the rule and passes
fields.statement: This repository turns the unclaimed-changes rule on: it commits .rhiza/check.json with unclaimed_since set to the origin/main commit the branch is built on when the file is written
